clue.text: Opens doors with a tiny movement, being graceful

indicators.note: what opens a word is its first letter, so only the start of the next word is kept
a movement shifts things about, so the letters of the phrase after 'with' get rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone nudges doors open with the slightest touch, in an elegant manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Dainty describes something delicate and elegant in movement or form, a close synonym for refined poise.

clue.text: Hop round first gap

indicators.note: the hopping word goes round, enclosing the next word

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance
1st, written with I for the numeral one

explanation.surface: An athlete's instruction: hop around the first opening.
explanation.walkthrough: A hop is an old word for a dance, as in a sock hop.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap is the space between two points, which is a distance.

clue.text: Poor Enid takes very little US money gross

indicators.note: poor in the sense of badly made, so the name is put in a different order

parts.note: a cent is the smallest US coin

explanation.surface: Poor Enid's US gross earnings are almost nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gross' sounds like total pay, matching the money; it means offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Gross in the sense of crude or obscene behaviour is offensive to decency, which is indecent.

clue.text: Strained to see numbers on key

explanation.surface: Someone peers hard to read the numbers on a keypad.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Tense describes nerves or muscles stretched tight, the same as strained or under stress.

clue.text: One forgets to become one

parts.note: surface reading: someone fails to remember to turn into something
setter's reading: a person who forgets is, by that very act, a sufferer of memory loss

explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on the circularity: forgetting is exactly what makes a person this, so the forgetting and the becoming are the same thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A person suffering from memory loss is called by this medical noun, so someone who forgets fits.

clue.text: Girl and journalist both ate out and lost the opportunity

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young woman

indicators.note: out in the sense of wrongly arranged, so these words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A young woman and a reporter dined out together and let a chance slip by.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being too late to take advantage of a chance, likened to arriving after departure.

clue.text: Conductor may choose soldier to take party back

indicators.note: the soldier takes in the party, holding it inside

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, stand for a soldier

indicators.note: back means the party word is turned to run the other way

explanation.surface: An orchestra leader picks a soldier to bring the band back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' suggests music; here it is an electrical one.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrode is an electrical conductor through which current enters or leaves a circuit.

clue.text: Work inside in back-street bars

indicators.note: the work word goes inside the other letters

parts.note: to go is to work or function

indicators.note: back says the street abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Someone toils away in the pubs of a back street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bars' looks like pubs; it means bars of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingots are cast blocks of metal such as gold, which are bars.

clue.text: Rush job?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to hurtle along out of control
second meaning: one's profession or working life

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an urgent piece of work; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to move swiftly and wildly; as a noun, one's occupation or life's work.

clue.text: From south of France article arrives here

definitions.note: a place: the country where the wordplay arrives

parts.note: sud is the French word for south

explanation.surface: Something travels up from the south of France and arrives at its destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South of France' reads as the Riviera; it asks for the French word for south. The definition is the bare word 'here', the place where the letters arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: The African country is a place, the destination pointed at by the adverb as a location reached by travellers.

clue.text: Hand green form to traveller

parts.note: to hand something is to pass it

indicators.note: to form something is to shape it, so the colour word is shaped into a new order

explanation.surface: An official hands a green document to someone on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone riding in a vehicle, train or plane without driving it is a person on a journey, a traveller.

clue.text: Salary joiner gets to veneer parking sign?

definitions.note: names the scheme a sign announces

parts.note: a veneer is an outward show or display

explanation.surface: A carpenter's wages get spent on veneer, hinted at by a car-park notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joiner' suggests a carpenter, which fits veneer; it is the word joining clauses. Pay and display is the British car-park system where you buy a ticket and leave it on view.
explanation.definitionFit: Car-park signs announcing this system tell drivers to buy a ticket and show it in the windscreen.

clue.text: Chief gets Jaguar car, an original model

parts.note: arch- as in archbishop means chief
the E-Type is a classic Jaguar sports car

explanation.surface: The boss treats themselves to a new Jaguar, a model from the original range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a car model; here it is the first pattern from which copies come.
explanation.definitionFit: An archetype is the first pattern or prototype from which all later copies derive.

clue.text: Heading for the French bird first

indicators.note: says the bird's word comes at the front, ahead of the French word

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: An instruction to put the bird first in a French heading.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is the heading placed at the top of a page, chapter or article.

clue.text: Northern comedian not worried about disapproval

indicators.note: worried in the old sense of shaken about, so the words before are jumbled

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A comic from the north shrugs off people's disapproval.
explanation.definitionFit: Condemnation is strong censure, the expression of severe disapproval of someone's conduct.

clue.text: Could be his paper taking note of inscriptions

indicators.note: suggests the letters could form something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: A man's paper might be taking notes on carved inscriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: Epigraphs are words carved on buildings or statues, or quotations heading a book.

clue.text: Serviceman stands in it on repairing firing system

indicators.note: in a down clue standing up means the serviceman is read from the bottom upward
repairing means putting back together, so those little words are reassembled

explanation.surface: A soldier stands in for someone repairing a gun's firing mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: The ignition is the mechanism in an engine that fires the fuel mixture with a spark.

clue.text: Heavenly present in a case of mixed ale!

indicators.note: a case holds something, so the first word sits within the other letters
mixed means the drink's letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: to be present is to be there

explanation.surface: A cheerful toast: a case of mixed beer is a gift from heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means light and otherworldly, of the celestial sphere, hence heavenly.

clue.text: Mean to clout boxer

parts.note: the mean is the middle value

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to land a blow on a fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clout' reads as a punch; it is influence.
explanation.definitionFit: A middleweight is a fighter in the weight division between welterweight and light heavyweight.

clue.text: Doctor returned as in charge of Moses

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the little word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A doctor returns as the person in charge of a man called Moses.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the adjective: Mosaic law is the law given by Moses.
explanation.definitionFit: Mosaic is the adjective relating to the prophet, as in the Mosaic law of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Bill for advertising?

parts.note: surface reading: an invoice for the cost of an ad campaign
setter's reading: a bill as a printed notice pasted up on a wall to advertise something

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' suggests a demand for payment; here it is the printed notice, as in bill-sticking.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed placard displayed in public to promote an event or product is a sheet stuck to walls.

clue.text: Love the same old city smell

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O
do is short for ditto, the same
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: A fond recollection of the familiar old town's stink.
explanation.definitionFit: An odour is a scent or whiff, especially a distinctive or unpleasant one.

clue.text: Horse Neil trained by the water's edge

indicators.note: training puts something into a new shape, so the two names are reshaped

explanation.surface: A racehorse is put through its paces by its trainer Neil along the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: The line where land meets sea or lake is the boundary at the coast, its edge.

clue.text: Spike left to meet youth leader in good time

parts.note: an ear is the spike of a cereal plant
L is the abbreviation for left

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter is kept

explanation.surface: Spike left promptly to meet the leader of a youth club.
explanation.walkthrough: An ear of corn or wheat is its spike of grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in good time means doing it ahead of schedule, before it is due.

clue.text: George found car with very good allowance

parts.note: pi, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for very good
one's lot is one's allotted share

explanation.surface: A man called George came across a car and a generous allowance.
explanation.walkthrough: George is old pilots' slang for the automatic pilot, so the man's name is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmen nicknamed the automatic flight control system George, a slang term for it.

clue.text: Recommend removing front of hoist

indicators.note: taking away the front means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: to recommend is to speak in favour of, to praise

explanation.surface: An instruction suggesting taking the front off a lifting device.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoist something is to lift it up, synonymous with elevating it.

clue.text: Respectful gestures making us cry, set off

indicators.note: off in the sense of gone bad or awry, so the preceding letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Bows of deference that set people off weeping.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtsey is a bob made by bending the knees, a polite sign of deference to royalty.

clue.text: Book him, say, having lost one nail

indicators.note: one is the roman numeral I, and losing it drops that letter from the word that follows
say asks for the pronoun as it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a song of praise sounds the same as this pronoun

explanation.surface: Arrest him, as it were, now that a fingernail has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a verb (to arrest); it is the noun. Nail without its I leaves NAL, and the setter runs it on so the N it starts with is shared with the end of HYMN.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymnal is a volume of church songs used by a congregation in worship.
